metadata.environment: Chrome headless (Playwright/patchright driver), Windows, localhost vite preview production build

lighthouse.runs: 3 cold runs per profile; Lighthouse 13.5.0; desktop preset / mobile simulate throttling
lighthouse.note: Local preview server (no network latency); values comparable with M3B.1 lab method but include run variance. Main-thread duration is not reported because the same aggregate was not extracted in M3B.1's artifacts with an identical method; TBT is the comparable metric.

comparisonToM3B1.desktopTbt: M3B.1 2,925 ms vs M3B.3 3,341 ms median (+416 ms, +14%). Single-run overlap: M3B.3 run 2 = 3,268 ms; M3B.1's own median derives from one source doc. The texture cache does not touch the startup path (textures generate on first render, which is post-LCP); no mechanism exists for the cache to add ~300-400 ms of TBT. Interpretation: run-to-run variance on a shared workstation, consistent with the M3A note that Lighthouse is dominated by startup variance. No regression claim can be made from a single 3-run comparison without repeating M3B.1 on the same day/machine state; flagged for re-measurement in the release review.
comparisonToM3B1.mobileTbt: M3B.1 13,125 ms vs M3B.3 14,314 ms median; run 2 = 13,071 ms is BELOW the M3B.1 median, confirming high run variance on mobile throttling.
comparisonToM3B1.scores: Desktop 47 -> 46, Mobile 31 -> 31: within Lighthouse run variance (±2 points documented in M1A/M2 history).

heap.performanceMemoryUsedJSHeapMB: measured per-session (varies 180-310 MB across Showroom sessions depending on canvas size and Chrome version); JS heap does not grow monotonically across rapid livery cycles (see rapidCycles task counts staying flat)
heap.gpuMemory: not reliably exposed by the browser in this environment; not claimed
